last.summary:
Approved. The change adds only the two allowed files (Compress/Mtf.lean and Test/CompressMtf.lean). `projects/bzip2/tools/verify.sh` passed when I ran it: verify: packages: ok; sources: ok; build: ok; style: ok; axioms: ok; lint: ok; test: ok; verify: ok. The task names no check-task script, and checks/ has no entry for it.

Behaviour checked against the C code:
- I built a C driver out of tree. It includes upstream/compress.c and calls generateMTFValues directly (ptr[i]=(i+1)%n, so the BWT column is the block itself). It reproduces the expected symbols, freqs and nInUse for banana, the 7-byte block {a,n,n,b,0,a,a}, abracadabra, 1000 zeros, 999 zeros + 1, six x then y, and six x alone. These are the same cases the #guards assert. The other run lengths (1-5) are consistent with the same flushRun logic and the tested boundaries.
- generateMtf does what compress.c:160-230 does: makeMaps_e numbering (compress.c:106-115), yy initialisation (161), the zPend increment when yy[0] matches (170-171), and the flush before an MTF move (172-187). It also matches the final flush (212-226) and the EOB append (228) with mtfFreq sized nInUse+2. The RUNA/RUNB loop (zPend-1, bit 0 gives RUNA/RUNB, then (z-2)/2) is the same, as is the MTF symbol j+1.
- The empty block gives [EOB=1] and freq [0,1]. This is safe in C and in Lean because yy is never read when the block is empty.
- All the cited line ranges exist and say what the text claims. compress.c:106-115 is makeMaps_e, 120-231 is generateMTFValues, and 170-188 and 212-226 are the two zPend flushes. bzlib.c:124, 223 and 238 are the inUse reset and the two places inUse is set, including the state_in_len-4 count byte.

Tests cover what the task lists: runs of 1-6 (mid-block and as the whole block), 1000 zeros, and one-byte-value blocks.

Notes, not required for approval:
- The module doc says the caller does the ptr indirection, so the API takes the already-permuted BWT column. That is a reasonable reading of 'from the BWT output' and the doc states it.
- Bytes missing from inUse silently map to symbol 0, as the doc comment notes; C would hit an AssertD there.
